lede: Your decision (feeds d41, at your Mon 10/19 review): which board and encoder the 5 s cut sheet should lock, and whether to map the full size curve (and real-Pi runs after pool test 2). Below: a 5 s moving-camera clip (Reef Check diver over kelp, Caspar, Oct 2025), scaled to 720p and encoded the way each board could do it, each at its rated frame rate: IMX708 30 fps, N6 15 fps, AE3 10 fps. Off-the-shelf encoders only, run on the Mac to imitate each board (desk emulation); no Pi or board runs. Drag a picture: left is the source, right is the encode; the chips switch encoders. Tap a picture for full screen and 1:1 zoom.

facts.label: the only board that encodes video by itself today (hardware H.264, real time)
its chip has H.264, but stock firmware doesn't use it: custom firmware needed
at 720p, software JPEG, no encoder hardware: 720p at 10 fps needs custom work
smallest 5 s 720p clip with MJPEG (AE3; N6 ≥ 1.3 MB), so 100 / 500 KB need a video codec
VMAF at 500 KB, 30 fps, worst clip: AV1 on the Pi vs H.264 (70 = good)

notes: Under 1 MB at 720p, every board needs a real video codec, and today that runs on the Pi: the IMX708 directly, the N6 by streaming its frames over USB. The AE3 can't deliver 720p at 10 fps to anything today.

At 500 KB per 5 s, AV1 on the Pi is 'good' (VMAF 71–77 on the worst clip at 30 / 15 / 10 fps) but costs ~2–8 min of Pi time per clip; H.264 is real time but scores 42 (IMX708, 30 fps) to 51 (N6 H.264, 15 fps, custom firmware) and smears moving kelp.
100 KB per 5 s (the Spotter size): nothing is watchable on moving-camera footage. AV1 on the Pi reaches 35–42 on the worst clip, H.264 under 5.

Smallest size with the most quality (the knee): bracketed at 500 KB–1 MB, not found below 1 MB. Every encoder that reaches 500 KB still gains 10–23 VMAF points (worst of 3 clips) from 500 KB to 1 MB. Locating it needs the full size curve (your call).

The AE3's MJPEG jumps from VMAF 34 at 769 KB to 81 at 996 KB (this clip). That is real: JPEG's size has a floor. At quality 5 or lower every quantizer is capped, so the file stops shrinking (769 / 770 / 789 KB at quality 1 / 3 / 5) while the picture keeps falling apart (VMAF 34 / 37 / 48). The last ~230 KB buys a lot (60 at 822 KB, 70 at 879 KB, 81 at 996 KB).
VMAF reads brightness only: the AE3's 1 MB MJPEG scores 81 on the primary clip but shows colour blotches at 1:1. Judge by eye.

Desk emulation: x264 'veryfast' stands in for hardware H.264. On the real Pi (10/02 bench), hardware H.264 scored ~10 VMAF below a good software H.264 at the same size, so the IMX708 H.264 here is probably flattering. The N6's real JPEG tables differ from libjpeg's.

Scores are relative to the Reef Check source, which is itself compressed (4K HEVC), and each board is scored at its own frame rate; VMAF ignores 10 fps choppiness. The AE3 720p / 10 fps pictures are hypothetical.
footer: Desk emulation on the Mac, Sat 10/17, per spec SPEC_e7_video_cutsheet rev 3 (rig PR #122, RESULTS.md). Windows picked by a rule committed before any encode: 3 Reef Check clips with camera motion (primary shown here), plus pool clips as a control. Pi time and energy are estimates from the 10/15 study (rig #116) and the 10/02 real-Pi bench (PR #88).
